import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales per product
sales_per_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product', as_index=False)['total'].sum()

# Set the aesthetics for the plot
sns.set(style='whitegrid')

# Create a bar plot for total sales per product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
bar_plot = sns.barplot(data=sales_per_product, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.title('Total Coffee Sales by Product', fontsize=16)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Create a new column for total sales per product
sales_per_product = coffee_sales.groupby('product', as_index=False)['total'].sum()

# Set the aesthetics for the plot
sns.set(style='whitegrid')

# Create a bar plot for total sales per product
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
bar_plot = sns.barplot(data=sales_per_product, x='total', y='product', palette='viridis')

# Add labels and title
plt.xlabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Product', fontsize=14)
plt.title('Total Coffee Sales by Product', fontsize=16)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
